dedupe_keys.name: seismic fragility functions of a tailings dam under subduction earthquakes bellido and aguilar csee 2024

description: This study derives seismic fragility functions for a tailings dam shaken by subduction earthquakes, using finite-difference simulations with advanced constitutive models in the FLAC software to predict horizontal crest displacement under ground motions compatible with the Maximum Credible Earthquake used in South American practice. The modelled dam has 100 m of tailings behind a 101 m rockfill embankment with a 10 m crest and downstream and upstream slopes of 2:1 and 1.5:1. Fragility curves are given for several intensity measures, including peak ground acceleration, Arias intensity and cumulative absolute velocity, and Arias intensity proves the most efficient predictor. It was written by Nestor Bellido and Zenón Aguilar of the National University of Engineering in Lima and presented at the 9th World Congress on Civil, Structural, and Environmental Engineering in London in April 2024. It concerns one dam configuration. The paper is available free online as a PDF with a DOI; no licence is stated. Caveats: results apply to the modelled geometry and materials, and the code used is commercial. For simulation it provides damage probabilities for tailings dams in subduction zones, feeding hazard exposure and resilience models of mines and downstream communities, water and roads. It is related to the Mount Polley tailings breach review case study record in this catalogue.
